subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class core/plugin responsibility-state contract for durable memory and evidence reuse, or should this remain an umbrella over narrower provenance and approval issues?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses persistent storage, plugin SDK contracts, approval semantics, config, UI/audit state, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent trust model safely.

options.title: Design a narrow trust contract
options.body: Define owner-confirmed lifecycle states and reuse-policy semantics once, then let memory/plugins implement that contract without duplicating approval logic.

options.title: Keep as umbrella only
options.body: Track this issue as the coordinating design thread while narrower issues land source provenance, persistence hooks, and approval improvements independently.

options.title: Route to external/plugin experiments
options.body: Keep SCBKR/UMP-style responsibility chains outside core unless a concrete missing OpenClaw plugin API blocks them.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow trust contract
recommendation.body: Define owner-confirmed lifecycle states and reuse-policy semantics once, then let memory/plugins implement that contract without duplicating approval logic.

likelyOwner.reason: The current memory/plugin contract files all route through recent work tied to this owner signal, and the decision likely starts at that API boundary before implementation.
